summary: Dedicated: latency spikes during peak traffic; needs standardized saturation context (GPU/queue/KV) for faster triage
description:
Issue summary:
Acme AI (Dedicated) reports intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes on chat completions during peak traffic windows. Spikes are large enough to cause upstream request timeouts in their app. Customer requests clearer, actionable saturation context for Dedicated pools (GPU/queue/KV cache pressure) and faster escalation guidance.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency spikes (p95 up to ~4–8s; p99 >10s reported by customer) for ~20–40 minute windows.
- Increased retry traffic observed from customer (amplifies load).
- No sustained elevated 5xx; primary symptom is latency + occasional streaming stalls.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in prod, us-east
- Pool: acme-ai-dedicated-us-east-1
- Models: llama-3-70b-instruct, qwen2.5-72b-instruct
- Request pattern: high concurrency, mix of 1–4k prompt tokens, 200–800 output tokens; streaming enabled for most traffic

Customer report (from CS call / email excerpts):
- "Everything is fine most of the day, but when we hit our morning peak we get sudden latency cliffs for 20–30 minutes. We can’t tell if it’s GPU saturation, queueing, or a bad rollout." 
- "We need to know what to look at during an incident: is it capacity, batching, or routing?" 

Initial hypothesis:
Likely saturation/queueing in Dedicated scheduler (admission control/backpressure) and/or KV cache pressure causing effective throughput collapse under long-context + high concurrency.

Gaps:
We do not currently surface a consistent 'saturation context' bundle for Dedicated pools in support workflows. The on-call investigation required ad-hoc dashboard hunting and manual correlation. This ticket tracks both the immediate incident handling and the follow-up requirement to standardize saturation signals + incident-bot context cards for Dedicated incidents.
comments: 2025-03-12 09:18 PT - Owen Phillips (Support): Created ticket from Acme AI escalation. Customer reports p95/p99 latency spikes starting ~08:40 PT. Asked for request IDs + timeframe + any recent config changes on their side.

2025-03-12 09:26 PT - Dev Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Pulling internal dashboards for acme-ai-dedicated-us-east-1 and checking for deploys/config pushes. Looping in SRE (Rafael Mendes) and Platform (Mina Haddad) for Dedicated pool saturation review.

2025-03-12 09:33 PT - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Looking at Dedicated pool metrics. GPU util appears high but not pegged; latency correlates more with scheduler queue depth spikes. Not enough visibility into KV cache pressure in the standard dashboard for this pool.

2025-03-12 09:41 PT - Dev Patel (Support): Customer confirms no app deploy at onset; traffic ramped as expected. Provided example timestamps: 08:42–09:10 PT, 09:15–09:22 PT. No changes to model pins today.

2025-03-12 09:55 PT - Jacob Stein (Diagnostics Eng): Quick triage: queue depth spikes align with longer prompts; suggests admission control/batching threshold mismatch or insufficient headroom. We need standardized saturation snapshot (GPU util + queue depth + backpressure + KV cache pressure) in one place for Dedicated.
2025-03-12 10:07 PT - Mina Haddad (Routing): Confirmed no routing policy changes affecting Acme Dedicated. This looks local to their pool; no evidence of cross-tenant impact.

2025-03-12 10:22 PT - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Mitigation suggestion: temporarily lower max concurrency per replica / adjust batching to reduce tail latency under KV pressure (trade throughput for predictability). Customer may prefer more predictable latency. Can we apply a temporary scheduler guardrail for this pool?

2025-03-12 10:35 PT - Ethan Park (Control Plane): We can apply a pool-level policy override (burst disabled, stricter queue limits) to prevent runaway queueing. Also recommend adding a short-term autoscaling bump if GPU headroom exists. Need confirmation of current reserved capacity ceiling.

2025-03-12 10:48 PT - Dev Patel (Support): Shared with customer: we’re seeing queue depth/backpressure spikes; we’ll apply guardrails to reduce tail latency and follow up with a root cause. Asked customer if they can tolerate slightly higher 429s vs timeouts (they prefer predictable latency; 429 acceptable if well-bounded).

2025-03-12 11:10 PT - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Applied temporary queue limit policy for acme-ai-dedicated-us-east-1 to cap queueing delay; observed p99 latency improve within ~10 minutes. GPU util remains high but stable; queue depth no longer spikes as severely.

2025-03-12 11:27 PT - Dev Patel (Support): Customer confirms improvement: p95 back down to ~1.2–1.8s, fewer timeouts. Keeping policy override in place for 24h while we investigate sustainable fix (capacity/batching settings).

2025-03-13 08:05 PT - Logan Wright (Telemetry): Noted we still lack a consistent KV cache pressure metric in the support-facing dashboard for Dedicated pools. There is ongoing work to standardize saturation signals; recommend referencing the saturation-signals standardization doc and incident-bot v2 cards once available.

2025-03-13 09:12 PT - Aisha Bello (SLO/Alerting): This incident is a good example of why we need actionable saturation thresholds. GPU util alone is insufficient; queue depth + backpressure should be the leading indicator. We can tune alerts to catch this earlier without noisy pages.

2025-03-14 14:20 PT - Dev Patel (Support): Follow-up with customer: We believe the spikes were due to queueing/backpressure under peak concurrency + long contexts. We applied queue guardrails. Next steps: add standardized saturation context (GPU/queue/KV/backpressure) and share guidance/runbook. Customer requests a 'single link' dashboard and incident snapshot for future spikes.

2025-03-17 10:03 PT - Jacob Stein (Diagnostics Eng): Action item proposal: Incident-bot v2 'Saturation signals' card should include Dedicated pool identifiers and show: GPU util (avg/max), scheduler queue depth (p95), backpressure/admission control rate, KV cache pressure (if available) + deep links. This aligns with the reliability initiative (Incident bot + diagnostics improvements).

2025-03-18 16:40 PT - Dev Patel (Support): Closing as resolved: symptoms mitigated via pool policy guardrails; customer stable. Keeping internal follow-up tracked via linked tickets (telemetry/query improvements and saturation signal standardization).
resolution:
Resolved.

What we did:
- Confirmed issue localized to Acme AI Dedicated pool in us-east.
- Observed scheduler queue depth/backpressure spikes correlating with reported latency cliffs; GPU util alone was not a reliable indicator.
- Applied temporary pool-level queue limit / guardrail to cap queueing delay and stabilize p95/p99 latency during peak.

Customer outcome:
- Customer reported immediate improvement and fewer upstream timeouts after guardrail change.

Follow-ups (tracked elsewhere):
- Standardize saturation signals for Dedicated pools (GPU util + queue depth + admission control/backpressure + KV cache pressure where available) and ensure there is a single support-friendly dashboard.
- Add/expand incident-bot v2 saturation context card to include Dedicated pool saturation snapshot + deep links (references: incident-bot diagnostics v2 design).

Notes:
- This ticket highlights the operational gap: support + on-call lacked a consistent, tenant-safe saturation context bundle. Investigation required ad-hoc correlation and manual dashboard navigation.
